# R371 v2 — Ryzen 5 5600X AVX2 expert decode: corrected type/byte audit and current NT scope

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). This v2 is a source-only correction of R371 v1. V1 remains unchanged. Fixed source is `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/diag-native-copy-queue-qualified-20261013`, HEAD `410904c99d273435b5302fa8976cc667d17957f2`. No Git, build, test, model, GPU, or service operation was performed. Only this v2 report was written. Pack inspection was limited to the text metadata `native_experts.txt`.

## Corrections that change the conclusion

V1 confused Q4_0 with Q2_0 and overstated native Q2_0 Down bytes 2×. In this GGML type enum, Q4_0 is type 2; Q2_0 is type 42. A Q2_0 block has QK=64 and 18 bytes (2-byte FP16 scale + 16 code bytes), not 36 bytes. For 2,560 Down rows with K=640, each row has 10 blocks, so Q2_0 Down is 2,560×10×18 = **460,800 B**, while IQ4_NL Down is 2,560×20×18 = **921,600 B**. This matches the exact native pack: layer 1 is GU type 22 / Down type 42 and blob_bytes=1,510,400 B = IQ2_S GU 1,049,600 B + Q2_0 Down 460,800 B. Q2_0 Down uses the local `ActQ` row kernel through `pool.cpp`, not `native_down_rows`; it does consume the intermediate activation quantized into `ActQ`. The NT5–8 duplicate-decode observation is real for the generic wrappers, but **cannot occur in the stated current decode configuration**: no MTP, `spec=0`, verifier T=1 means the decode dispatch supplies one token row, so each expert job has NT=1 (top-10 IDs are unique within a token). The read-window ring width 16 is a separate buffering dimension and does not make `ExpertJobMulti.nt` 16. Remove NT5–8 from current-target priorities; it only merits study for a different route that actually supplies five or more token rows in one expert dispatch.

## Full 48-layer metadata audit

The installed pack header reports native format v3, 512 experts, 48 layers, total 50,292,326,400 B. All 48 rows were read as text and grouped by `(gu_type, d_type)`; their per-expert blob sum is 98,227,200 B, which times 512 equals the header total exactly. In one-token decode, top-10 route extent at all 48 layers remains the R369 v2 logical value 982,272,000 B (936.767578 MiB) if all selected IDs are CPU misses. This is a logical packed-source extent, never measured DRAM traffic.

| native GGML types | pack interpretation | layer count | blob bytes/layer | summed bytes for one expert across those layers |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 18 / 20 | IQ3_XXS GU / IQ4_NL Down | 14 | 2,176,000 | 30,464,000 |
| 18 / 42 | IQ3_XXS GU / Q2_0 Down | 3 | 1,715,200 | 5,145,600 |
| 21 / 20 | IQ3_S GU / IQ4_NL Down | 9 | 2,329,600 | 20,966,400 |
| 21 / 42 | IQ3_S GU / Q2_0 Down | 1 | 1,868,800 | 1,868,800 |
| 22 / 20 | IQ2_S GU / IQ4_NL Down | 15 | 1,971,200 | 29,568,000 |
| 22 / 42 | IQ2_S GU / Q2_0 Down | 5 | 1,510,400 | 7,552,000 |
| 23 / 20 | IQ4_XS GU / IQ4_NL Down | 1 | 2,662,400 | 2,662,400 |
| **all** | | **48** | | **98,227,200** |

This census corrects the oversimplified use of the pack name “IQ3_S”: only 10 GU layers are IQ3_S; 20 are IQ2_S, 17 IQ3_XXS, and one IQ4_XS. The requested kernel table below covers IQ3_XXS/IQ2_S/IQ3_S GU and IQ4_NL/Q2_0 Down, but the real pack also has a single IQ4_XS GU layer. Native type ID 42 is Q2_0 in the source's GGML fork. The upstream GGML primary enum independently confirms Q4_0=2 and Q2_0=42.

## Corrected expert math and bytes

All rows use the full inner dimension. For H=2560 and FF=640, each GU projection has 640 rows × 10 IQ blocks of 256 values. Both gate and up are evaluated. Down has 2,560 rows × 640 inputs. Each product count is independent of the weight encoding.

| phase | format and block | blocks/row | rows | packed bytes/expert | products/expert-token |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GU (both projections) | IQ2_S, 256 values / 82 B | 10 | 1,280 | 1,049,600 | 3,276,800 |
| GU (both projections) | IQ3_XXS, 256 / 98 B | 10 | 1,280 | 1,254,400 | 3,276,800 |
| GU (both projections) | IQ3_S, 256 / 110 B | 10 | 1,280 | 1,408,000 | 3,276,800 |
| Down | IQ4_NL, 32 / 18 B | 20 | 2,560 | 921,600 | 1,638,400 |
| Down | Q2_0, 64 / 18 B | 10 | 2,560 | **460,800** | 1,638,400 |

For the requested combinations, total packed expert extent is 1,510,400–2,329,600 B: examples are IQ2_S+Q2_0 = 1,510,400 B, IQ3_XXS+IQ4_NL = 2,176,000 B, IQ3_S+IQ4_NL = 2,329,600 B, and IQ3_S+Q2_0 = 1,868,800 B. All seven type pairs' exact totals agree with the metadata table. Work is 4,915,200 weight×activation products, conventionally 9,830,400 multiply-add FLOPs, excluding codebook/index operations, activation quantization, block scaling/corrections, SiLU and reductions.

The Q2_0 Down activation is not GGML Q8_1. `pool.cpp:491-494` sends FF through `act_quant_any` when `d_type==42`; `:344-349` builds `ActQ* a2` and passes it to `q2_rows_any`. With the default Q2 bitplane route, the row kernel reads `qp`, `psum`, and `pscale`; quantizer preparation also fills the base q/scale/sum/hx and creates the plane image. At FF=640, active populated fields are 640+80+80+80+640+160+160 = about 1,840 B, excluding struct padding. `expert.hpp:67-80` reserves a much larger fixed H-sized struct; active data size is not allocated struct size and neither is DDR traffic. For comparison, GGML Q8_K GU activation is 10×292=2,920 B/token and IQ4_NL Q8_0 Down activation is 20×34=680 B/token. These inputs feed many rows and are likely repeatedly accessed; cache residency is unmeasured.

## What the current decode route can do

The active measurement configuration has no MTP, `spec=0`, verifier T=1. From generate's pool callback, `n_tok` is passed directly to `expert_pool_dispatch_multi`. In `expert_source.cpp`, a job is created once per expert; each routed row appends one activation/output pointer and increments that job's `nt`. The native top-k router marks each winner as taken before the next rank, so one token has unique top-10 IDs. Therefore its `ExpertJobMulti.nt` is exactly 1 for CPU-missed jobs in this decode configuration. The verifier/read-window machinery's ring width 16 is a queue capacity, not a value passed as `n_tok` and not a multiplier for job.nt. Prompt windows with multiple rows have a different shape; that does not make NT5+ a decode candidate for this run.

Thus the Down wrappers' NT5–8 behavior is currently irrelevant: `iq_avx2_rows.inl:240-250`, `:320-330` and `q2_avx2_rows.inl:54-66` split those calls into groups of four, decoding each weight block once per group. GU dispatch at `:224-235` supports NT5–8 directly. This v2 keeps the source observation as an out-of-scope prompt/grouped route possibility only. **Do not prioritize, implement or benchmark it for the stated decode target.** If a later target increases verifier rows, consult the already available `CpuJobHistogram` (`expert_source.cpp:1415-1440`) and require actual NT5–8 incidence before reopening.

## Measurement order for the actual target

1. Use existing per-request CPU phase wall counters for GU, FF activation quantization and Down, together with per-format routed expert count and actual job.nt histogram. At T=1 this means NT1 is the decode cell. Do not use prompt-batch counts or ring width as a proxy. Existing counters are host phase envelopes and can overlap GPU execution; they are not additive end-to-end critical-path time.
2. Within the dominant phase, compare same format/shape with a compact reused expert set and a larger rotating set. Record pinned participant count, task fragments, per-thread CPU time/cycles and LLC misses when low observer-cost counters are already available. A same-address vs rotating-set timing separates cache sensitivity but neither gives physical DRAM bytes. Only a memory-controller counter can support a DRAM traffic claim.
3. If GU dominates, measure IQ2_S, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S individually. Existing scalar/gather variants are not predictably ordered across formats, and Ryzen's default scalar choice is not evidence it is optimal. The existing source comments cite Intel CPUs, not this target. Compare exact NT1 CPU phase and total request; avoid changing activation arithmetic.
4. If quantization is material, isolate the one-time H=2560 input conversion from the per CPU-job FF=640 intermediate conversion. Do not attribute input conversion once per expert: it is one per token/layer before jobs. Q2_0's planar ActQ path is separate from the native IQ activation path.
5. Review worker5/tasks18 only if phase traces show underfill or tail imbalance. The pool partitions flattened expert rows into tasks; worker count, caller participation, task fragments and token count are different quantities. Thread count alone does not diagnose memory bandwidth saturation.
6. Keep FP32 recurrence state and all weight/activation quantization fixed. No 256K quality qualification exists for changing numerical paths. Do not extrapolate the logical top-10 packed extent to physical DDR bytes or declare 70 tok/s impossible from it.

The inputs above establish a minimal source-driven measurement plan, not a speed forecast. Current evidence does not decide whether IQ decode, integer dot/accumulator issue, act quantization, Down, row scheduling or DDR traffic dominates the end-to-end decode critical path.

## External implementation review (opened primary sources)

- The [GGML type enum](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/include/ggml.h) shows Q4_0=2, IQ3_XXS=18, IQ3_S=21, IQ2_S=22, IQ4_NL=20, and Q2_0=42 (opened enum lines 2864–2944). The [GGML block structs](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-common.h) define Q2_0 as 64 values with a two-byte half scale and 16 codes (18 B), IQ3_XXS as 98 B, IQ2_S as 82 B, IQ3_S as 110 B, and IQ4_NL as 18 B. GGML CPU traits map IQ3_XXS/IQ3_S/IQ2_S to Q8_K activation and IQ4_NL to Q8_0 in [ggml-cpu.c](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c).
- KTransformers' [cache-friendly AMX discussion](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/ktransformers/blob/main/doc/en/AMX.md) describes sharing activation data and partitioning expert work to use cache hierarchy. That is a measurement-design cue only; its AMX kernel/CPU setup is inapplicable to Ryzen 5600X AVX2.
- A [KTransformers AVX2 MXFP4 commit](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/ktransformers/commit/9481291) uses a four-token group to amortize weight decode and bounds a large per-expert path to control staging/register use. Its format is MXFP4 and its reported performance is on dual EPYC 7452; the transferable point is bounded token tiling around decode reuse, already present in Strata's IQ GU. It does not motivate an NT5+ change in the present T=1 route.
- The opened [vLLM CPU guide](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/getting_started/installation/cpu.md) describes the general CPU backend but does not present a directly substitutable IQ3/IQ2 CPU MoE decoder. The opened [SGLang expert-parallel guide](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/advanced_features/expert_parallelism.mdx) describes distributed EP runner/dispatch backends, not this local AVX2 IQ row kernel. [Intel LLM Scaler](https://github.com/intel/llm-scaler) identifies its solution as running on Intel Arc Pro B60/B70; I found no compatible Ryzen IQ kernel in the opened source surface. No claims about IPEX code were used because its requested page did not open successfully.
- These sources support implementation descriptions and transfer boundaries. No external benchmark is treated as a 5600X result.

## Prior-report delta and limits

R263 already listed IQ3_S gather, paired GU, IQ4_NL NT1, and kernel/service attribution. R224 already covered IQ2_S multi-token decode sharing and NT4 register pressure. R83 already warned about IQ2_S reduction-order differences. R173/R284 specify phase/job instrumentation. R369v2 establishes the corrected logical top-10 extent and explicitly does not measure physical DRAM. This v2 adds a corrected full 48-layer metadata/blob audit, fixes the Q2_0 type/block/down-byte mistake, verifies that Q2 Down uses ActQ, and rules the NT5–8 Down observation out of the stated T=1 decode path. No new optimization is adopted.

Still unknown are the per-format phase split, sustained 5600X service, LLC/DRAM receipts, pool CPU contribution, and full 256K quality. The correct current action is measurement at NT1 in the actual active type pairs, then rank only candidates supported by repeated end-to-end evidence. Keep state precision and model quality unchanged.
